samples.summary: Cycle guard added to three parent-chain walks, but the walks in `normalizeRange()` itself — same file, same render path, same map — are still unbounded `while` loops
samples.evidence: The change justifies its new `seen` sets with an explicit threat model: "Block ids arrive verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes (`crdt-tree.ts`), so a parent chain that loops back on itself — a duplicated or hostile id — is representable ... an unbounded one would hang the tab" (table-layout.ts:480-486). If that model holds, it is not fully mitigated: `normalizeRange()` in the very file being edited walks the same `layout.blockParentMap` with no visited set at selection.ts:147-151 (`while (anchorTopId && layout.blocks.findIndex(...) === -1) { ... anchorTopId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`) and again at selection.ts:153-157 for the focus. A two-node cycle (`a -> b -> a`, neither in `layout.blocks`) never satisfies the `findIndex(...) === -1` exit and never hits a missing parent, so the loop spins forever. `normalizeRange()` runs on every render/selection read (selection.ts:566, text-editor.ts:4322), i.e. it is reached before the guarded `resolveNestedTableLayout` is. That the repo already treats cyclic parent maps as real is visible in model/range-slices.ts:74-91, which carries exactly this `seen` guard ("bounds a parent map left cyclic by a stale layout"). A guard added at three of five sibling call sites reads as covered while the reachable path stays hangable.

samples.summary: `resolvePositionPixel` walks the same parent map with an unguarded `while (true)` — and it is driven once per remote peer cursor per render
samples.evidence: peer-cursor.ts:121-127 is the identical walk the diff hardened elsewhere (`let currentTableId = cellInfo.tableBlockId; while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(currentTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; nestingPath.unshift(parentInfo); currentTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`) with no `seen` set. Worse than the guarded sites, a cycle here also grows `nestingPath` without bound, so it is an unbounded allocation as well as an infinite loop — a memory-exhaustion/hang of every viewer, not only of a user who selects cells. This is the path that renders *peer* cursors, i.e. the one most directly fed by remote state, which is precisely the attacker the diff's own comment names. Not changed by this diff, but it is the sibling that makes the newly added guards incomplete.

samples.summary: `resolveCellGesture` calls throwing `doc.getBlock()` with ids taken from a possibly stale layout map, and the shift+click handler newly reaches it
samples.evidence: `Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found` (model/document.ts:226-240). `resolveCellGesture` calls it at text-editor.ts:3965 (`this.doc.getBlock(anchorTableId).tableData`) and 3989 (`this.doc.getBlock(resolveTableId).tableData`) with ids derived from `layout.blockParentMap`/hit-testing, which the codebase elsewhere documents as able to lag the document after remote edits ("Stale blockParentMap data (e.g. table rows removed by remote edit)", text-editor.ts:3028). Until this change the shift+click branch (text-editor.ts:2093-2095) never called `getBlock` on a table id; now a remote peer deleting a table between layout and the local user's shift+click raises an uncaught exception inside the `mousedown` handler. Remote-triggered client exception; low confidence because I could not confirm a concrete window where the map outlives the block. Use `findBlock` (document.ts:245, the non-throwing variant) here.
searchedFor: grep stale blockParentMap comments in text-editor.ts

samples.summary: `targetCell.blocks[0].id` assumes a cell always has at least one block; a remote-emptied cell makes the new gesture path throw
samples.evidence: Both `cells` returns dereference `targetCell.blocks[0].id` (text-editor.ts:3981 and 4000) after only checking that `targetCell` itself exists. `TableCell.blocks` is peer-writable content; a cell whose block list arrives empty yields `undefined.id` → TypeError in the `mousedown`/`mousemove` handler. Every neighbouring index access in the same function was defensively rewritten to `?.` in this change (rows/cells at 3975 and 3995), so the remaining unchecked `[0]` looks like an oversight rather than an invariant the code relies on elsewhere.

samples.summary: Read-time merge expansion (with its quadratic `findMergeTopLeft` scan) is now reachable per-render for nested tables, widening a known cost amplifier fed by peer-written spans
samples.evidence: `normalizeRange()` previously skipped `expandCellRangeForMerges` for nested tables because the flat lookup returned `undefined`; selection.ts:128-130 now resolves them, so the fixed-point loop at selection.ts:65-91 runs on every render for a nested-table cell rectangle, and it calls `findMergeTopLeft` (selection.ts:28-47, an O(rows x cols) scan) once per covered cell inside the rectangle. Spans are banded at `MAX_TABLE_SPAN = 1000` and columns at `MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS = 256` (model/numeric-attrs.ts:92,95), which is why this is bounded rather than a hang — but row counts are not obviously banded, and the same file explicitly names this loop as the DoS sink for peer-written spans (numeric-attrs.ts:205-211). Worth confirming the worst-case cost of the newly-enabled per-render path on a peer-supplied table with many covered cells.
searchedFor: grep normalizeTableSpan / MAX_TABLE_SPAN / MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS in packages/docs/src

samples.summary: Nested-table layout recursion has no depth cap, unlike the clipboard paste path which bounds it with MAX_TABLE_DEPTH
samples.evidence: `layoutCellBlocks` recurses into `computeTableLayout` for every nested table (table-layout.ts:132-145) with no depth parameter or ceiling, so a deeply nested table tree from the CRDT blows the stack on every render (RangeError, document unrenderable). The paste boundary already bounds exactly this (`depth >= MAX_TABLE_DEPTH`, view/clipboard.ts:308), so the CRDT read boundary is the unbounded one. Pre-existing and outside the diff, but it is the same peer-supplied-nesting threat the new cycle guards were added for, and it fires before those guards can help.
searchedFor: grep MAX_TABLE_DEPTH / maxDepth / nestDepth in packages/docs/src

finding.evidence: The change justifies its new `seen` sets with an explicit threat model: "Block ids arrive verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes (`crdt-tree.ts`), so a parent chain that loops back on itself — a duplicated or hostile id — is representable ... an unbounded one would hang the tab" (table-layout.ts:480-486). If that model holds, it is not fully mitigated: `normalizeRange()` in the very file being edited walks the same `layout.blockParentMap` with no visited set at selection.ts:147-151 (`while (anchorTopId && layout.blocks.findIndex(...) === -1) { ... anchorTopId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`) and again at selection.ts:153-157 for the focus. A two-node cycle (`a -> b -> a`, neither in `layout.blocks`) never satisfies the `findIndex(...) === -1` exit and never hits a missing parent, so the loop spins forever. `normalizeRange()` runs on every render/selection read (selection.ts:566, text-editor.ts:4322), i.e. it is reached before the guarded `resolveNestedTableLayout` is. verdict.reason: The absence is real and verified. selection.ts:147-151 and 153-157 walk layout.blockParentMap with plain `while` loops whose only exits are "id found in layout.blocks" or "no parent entry" — a cycle among ids absent from layout.blocks satisfies neither, so the loop spins. The three sibling walks over the same map ARE guarded with `seen` sets (table-layout.ts:488-494, text-editor.ts:3894-3906, text-editor.ts:3919-3924), and model/range-slices.ts:81-88 carries the same guard for doc.blockParentMap, so the inconsistency is exactly as described. I searched repo-wide for `seen|visited|new Set<string>` and `cycl|MAX_.*DEPTH|depth` in packages/docs/src: every guard hit is one of those four; clipboard.ts:71 (MAX_TABLE_DEPTH) and numeric-attrs.ts:111 (MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH) bound clipboard/attribute recursion, not parent-chain walks. I also checked all callers (selection.ts:562, 741, 755; text-editor.ts:501/3378/4165/4322/4363; editor.ts:2098-2154, 4059; text-box-editor.ts:566) and the map builders (table-layout.ts:146-150, 421-431; layout.ts:464, 514-517; editor.ts:1696-1703) — none validates or de-cycles the map first, so there is no caller-level or construction-level guard either. peer-cursor.ts:114-123 is a fifth unguarded walk of the same shape. The repo's own tests (nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:244-270) assert cycle-bailout only for resolveNestedTableLayout, never for normalizeRange, which runs earlier on the same render/selection path. Caveat recorded honestly: I could not construct a concretely cyclic single-pass body-layout map (post-order writes at table-layout.ts:423-431 rewrite a direct child's parent to its true tree parent), so end-to-end exploitability via the body layout is unproven; but the merged body+header+footer map (editor.ts:1696-1702) combines independently-built maps keyed by peer-controlled, duplicable ids, and the repo itself documents cyclic parent maps as reachable ("left cyclic by a stale layout", range-slices.ts:77). Untrusted-peer-input-driven unbounded looping on the render path is in-lane as unsafe input handling / availability; severity reflects impact if real.

finding.summary: `resolvePositionPixel` walks the same parent map with an unguarded `while (true)` — and it is driven once per remote peer cursor per render
finding.evidence: peer-cursor.ts:121-127 is the identical walk the diff hardened elsewhere (`let currentTableId = cellInfo.tableBlockId; while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(currentTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; nestingPath.unshift(parentInfo); currentTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`) with no `seen` set. Worse than the guarded sites, a cycle here also grows `nestingPath` without bound, so it is an unbounded allocation as well as an infinite loop — a memory-exhaustion/hang of every viewer, not only of a user who selects cells. This is the path that renders *peer* cursors, i.e. the one most directly fed by remote state, which is precisely the attacker the diff's own comment names. Not changed by this diff, but it is the sibling that makes the newly added guards incomplete.

verdict.reason: The claimed evidence checks out verbatim: peer-cursor.ts:119-127 walks layout.blockParentMap in a `while (true)` loop with no visited/`seen` set, and unshifts into `nestingPath` on every iteration, so a looping parent chain both spins forever and allocates without bound. I searched for a counterexample guard and found none: peer-cursor.ts contains no `seen`/`visited` set, and none of the call sites pre-validate the chain — editor.ts:2034-2046 passes remote `peer.position` straight in once per peer per render, cursor.ts:73 and selection.ts:276-277 likewise, and selection.ts:146-157 (the normalizing path) itself performs unguarded parent walks rather than acting as a gate. The repository's own comment at table-layout.ts:480-486 establishes the threat model and attacker: block ids "arrive verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes", so "a duplicated or hostile id" chain is representable and an unbounded walk "would hang the tab"; that site and text-editor.ts:3894/3919 were hardened with `seen`, leaving peer-cursor.ts as the unguarded sibling on the most directly remote-fed path. This is a remote-input-triggered availability/resource-exhaustion weakness (unsafe handling of untrusted peer-supplied identifiers) reachable with no local user interaction, so I keep it rather than dismissing it as pure correctness.

finding.summary: Unbounded `while (true)` parent-chain walk in `resolveNestedTableLayout` is newly reachable from the cell-range paint path; a peer-crafted document with duplicate block IDs can make the walk loop forever (tab hang).
finding.evidence: `resolveNestedTableLayout` walks up `layout.blockParentMap` in `while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(topTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; topTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }` (table-layout.ts:479-484) with no visited-set and no depth cap. Block IDs are taken verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes — `id: attrs.id ?? ''` (crdt-tree.ts:233 and :263) — and nothing in the repo validates uniqueness (grep for `duplicate|unique id|dedupe|seenIds` under packages/docs/src finds no ID-uniqueness check). `computeTableLayout` step 7 writes `blockParentMap.set(block.id, { tableBlockId, ... })` for each cell child including nested table blocks (table-layout.ts:423-431), so two nested tables that share IDs with each other's ancestors produce a chain A->B->A; the map is a flat Map keyed by ID, so last-writer-wins collisions are attacker-shapeable. Attack: a malicious collaborator (or a crafted document served to the victim) writes a nested-table structure with colliding block IDs; the victim drag-selects or shift+clicks cells in that table; the new line `resolveNestedTableLayout(crBlockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData` at selection.ts:130 runs on every `normalizeRange`, i.e. every render, and spins in the loop with the main thread pinned — an unrecoverable UI hang, no error surfaced. Note the same loop is already reachable from selection.ts:169 and from `buildCellRangeRects`, so this is an added reachability rather than a wholly new vector; I could not construct the exact CRDT tree that yields the cycle from the tests, hence low confidence. Fix is cheap: bound the walk with a visited `Set` (or a depth counter) and return `undefined` on a cycle, as the adjacent per-segment walk at selection.ts:147-157 also lacks.

verdict.reason: The finding's core assertion is factually wrong about the current tree. `resolveNestedTableLayout` does NOT have an unguarded walk: packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:488 declares `const seen = new Set<string>([topTableId])` and line 492 does `if (seen.has(parentInfo.tableBlockId)) return undefined;` inside the `while (true)` at 489-495 — exactly the visited-set fix the finding prescribes. The quoted evidence block (loop body with only `if (!parentInfo) break; topTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId;`) does not match the file. The comment at 480-486 spells out the same threat model (ids arriving verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes, walk now running once per painted cell rect) as the reason the guard was added. The follow-on descent at 516-523 re-walks the chain the guard just proved finite and acyclic, so it also terminates. Behavior is pinned by tests: test/view/nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:251-261 (a->b->a cycle) and 263-269 (self-referential id) both assert `undefined`. `grep "export function resolveNestedTableLayout"` returns exactly one definition (table-layout.ts:474), so the call site at selection.ts:130 cannot reach an unguarded variant; the sibling parent-chain walks at text-editor.ts:3894-3906 and 3918-3925 carry the same visited-set guard. Hence the claimed hang (cycle -> infinite spin -> pinned main thread) cannot occur; the walk bails to `undefined`. The only accurate part is the aside that selection.ts:147-157 lacks a visited set, but that is a different function and is not the defect the finding asserts; additionally a client-side hang is an availability concern outside the security lens's enumerated lane (authz, secrets, injection, crypto/auth, SSRF/deserialization/traversal).
